main.label: good
main.text: The loop visits each character and adds one to words every time it sees a space. For 'the quick brown fox' there are three spaces and words starts at 1, so the result is 4. It counts the separators and adds one for the first word.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: It never looks at the letters themselves, only the spaces. With three spaces between four words that gives 1 + 3 = 4, which is correct for this input.

main.label: good
main.text: words starts at 1 because a sentence with n words has n - 1 separating spaces, so counting the spaces and adding one gives n. Starting at 0 would give 3 for the four-word sentence, one too few.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: The extra 1 stands for the first word, which has no space in front of it. That only holds when the text is not empty and the words are separated by single spaces.

main.label: good
main.text: countWords(b) sees two spaces in 'hello  world', so it returns 3, but there are only two words, so that is wrong. countWords(c) on the empty string has no spaces and returns 1, but the correct answer is 0. So the function has a bug: it does not handle repeated spaces or empty input.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: I would say the function does not handle those cases. It would need to count transitions from a space to a letter, or skip repeated spaces, and return 0 for an empty string.

main.label: good
main.text: With a leading space, for example ' hello', the loop counts that space, so words becomes 2 even though there is one word. Every space is counted wherever it appears, so leading or trailing spaces add an extra word.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: It is the same reason as the double space: the code counts spaces, not words. A trailing space would add one too.

main.label: good
main.text: isLetter returns true for a character between a and z or between A and Z. countLetters loops over each char in the string and increments letters when isLetter is true, so spaces and digits are skipped. For 'the quick brown fox' that counts 16 letters.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: The range comparisons use the ASCII values of the characters, so punctuation and digits are not counted either, only the 52 letters.
